offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Regional Manager: Fleet

## 1. Your offer from Absa Group

Dear {{employee.full_name}},

We are pleased to offer you the position of Regional Manager: Fleet at Absa Group. This is a permanent role. Your employment will start on 1 December 2026.

## 2. Your role

You will lead regional sales and customer growth across Corporate, SME and Public Sector markets. You will manage a team of consultants, build and protect the customer portfolio, and work with Credit, Risk, Product, Operations, Finance, Legal and Customer Relations teams. You will also ensure records are kept correctly and that customer information is handled under POPIA.

## 3. Where and when you will work

Your place of work is Johannesburg, head office. You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break after no more than five hours of work.

## 4. Your pay and probation

You will earn R18,000.00 a month, paid on the 25th by EFT. The first 3 months of your employment are a probation period, during which we will assess your performance.

## 5. Next steps

Please bring your ID and qualifications when you accept this offer. This offer expires on 2026-11-30. Contact us at hr@example.co.za if you have questions.

I accept this offer of employment: {{employee.full_name}}, on {{date_signed}}.

Lead the team through the full sales lifecycle, including needs analysis, solution design, pricing, proposal development, negotiation, closure and implementation handover.; Achieve regional new business production, revenue, margin and market-share objectives within approved pricing, credit and risk parameters.; Own the health, retention and growth of the regional customer portfolio with the same level of focus as new business acquisition.; Implement a structured customer engagement model, including relationship plans, regular business reviews, service performance reviews and executive engagement for priority customers.; Identify and convert cross-sell, upsell, renewal and fleet expansion opportunities to increase customer share of wallet across AVMS products and value-added services.; Monitor customer satisfaction, complaints, service risks and early-warning indicators; coordinate timely service recovery and root-cause resolution to prevent attrition.; Maintain clear retention and growth plans for customers at risk, strategic accounts and high-potential portfolios.; Lead, coach and performance-manage a regional team of consultants accountable for acquisition, relationship management, retention and portfolio growth.; Allocate customer portfolios, prospects and regional opportunities to ensure clear ownership, appropriate capacity and balanced coverage.; Set individual and team targets and maintain a disciplined management rhythm covering pipeline, customer plans, renewals, service issues, wallet-growth opportunities and forecast accuracy.; Build capability in consultative selling, fleet and leasing solutions, commercial acumen, negotiation, customer engagement and service recovery.; Create a high-performance, customer-led culture with clear accountability, collaboration and succession planning.; Maintain a consolidated regional view of pipeline, portfolio performance, customer profitability, retention risk, wallet growth and service trends.; Use customer, operational and financial insights to prioritise interventions and implement corrective action where performance is below plan.; Ensure accurate forecasting, CRM discipline, management reporting and escalation of material commercial or customer risks.; Balance customer outcomes, commercial returns and risk when making regional decisions.; Coordinate Credit, Risk, Product, Operations, Finance, Legal and Customer Relations stakeholders to deliver integrated customer solutions and resolve regional delivery constraints.; Ensure seamless onboarding and implementation of new customers, with clear handover, service commitments and accountability.; Represent the voice of the customer in product, process and service-improvement forums and provide market intelligence to shape AVMS propositions.; Ensure adherence to Absa policies, sales governance, delegated authorities and applicable regulatory requirements.; Maintain complete and accurate approvals, customer records and deal documentation throughout the customer lifecycle.; Manage customer information in accordance with POPIA and relevant legislation and promptly escalate conduct, service, operational and reputational risks.. ## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Regional Manager: Fleet. plain_language.explanation: This clause names the two sides of the contract: Absa Group as the employer, based at 1 Main Road, Johannesburg, and you as the employee. It confirms your identity details and address will be recorded in the contract.

You are being hired as Regional Manager: Fleet, and this clause lists all your duties, including planning regional sales, managing the customer portfolio, leading and coaching your team, working with other departments, and following company policy and POPIA. The employer can also ask you to do other reasonable tasks that fit this role.
Your job starts on 1 December 2026 and it is a permanent position, meaning it has no fixed end date.

Your first 3 months are a trial period where your employer checks if you are doing the job well. You will get fair guidance and training during this time, and any decision to confirm, extend or end your employment after probation must follow a fair process.
You will work at the Johannesburg head office.

You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break after working five hours straight, plus at least 12 hours of rest between workdays and at least 36 hours of rest each week.

You will be paid R18,000.00 each month as your basic salary, which works out to R103.85 per hour. You are paid on the 25th of each month by EFT. You will not receive any other cash payments or payments in kind.

You only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot go over 10 hours a week. Overtime pay is 1.5 times your normal hourly rate, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. Sunday work is paid double your normal wage (or 1.5 times if you usually work Sundays), and public holiday work is paid double.

Your employer will deduct PAYE (tax) and 1% UIF from your pay. No other money will be taken from your salary unless you agree to it in writing, or the law, a court, or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave each year, to be taken when agreed with your employer and used within 6 months after the leave year ends. You get 30 days of paid sick leave every 36 months, but in your first 6 months you earn 1 day for every 26 days worked; your employer can ask for a doctor's note if you're off more than 2 days in a row or more than twice in 8 weeks. You are entitled to at least 4 months of maternity leave, 10 consecutive days of parental leave, adoption or commissioning leave as the law provides, and 3 days of paid family responsibility leave per year once you have worked more than 4 months and at least 4 days a week.

Either you or your employer can end the contract with written notice: 1 week if you've worked 6 months or less, 2 weeks if you've worked between 6 months and a year, and 4 weeks if you've worked more than a year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. Your employer can still dismiss you immediately for a serious reason if a fair process is followed, and both sides can agree to skip the notice period.
No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination covers your employer's business, so none of those extra rules apply to your job.
You must not share or use the employer's, clients', or suppliers' confidential information, whether you are still working there or have left, unless it's needed for your job or required by law.
No other documents are part of this contract besides what is written here.

This contract is the complete agreement between you and your employer, and any changes must be written down and signed by both of you. If any part of this contract gives you less than what the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or another relevant law provides, the better condition will apply instead. Your employer will keep your employment records for 3 years after you leave, and will explain these terms to you if you ask.
This is the signature section. Both the employer's signatory and you, the employee, must sign here to confirm you agree to this contract.
